pairs.question: An invenisti Bacchidem?
pairs.derivation: Chrysalus asks Pistoclerus directly. Dropped the framing interjection 'Eho,' that opens Chrysalus's line; the genuine interrogative is 'an invenisti Bacchidem?'. Pistoclerus answers 'Samiam quidem' (the Samian one, yes). Answer ends at the full stop; the next line begins a new directive ('Vide quaeso, ne quis tractet illam indiligens').

pairs.question: Benene usque valuit?
pairs.derivation: Nicobulus asks about his son Mnesilochus (established in the immediately preceding lines 'ubinamst Mnesilochus? ... Venitne?'); the -ne interrogative 'benene usque valuit?' asks whether he stayed well throughout. Chrysalus answers with the vivid 'pancratice atque athletice' (athletically and like a champion). Answer is the whole one-line reply; next line is a new question from Nicobulus ('Quid hoc?').

pairs.question: Quis istic Theotimust?
pairs.answer: Megalobuli filius, qui nunc in Ephesost Ephesiis carissimus.
pairs.derivation: Nicobulus asks who Theotimus is (named in the preceding lines as the priest with whom the gold was deposited). Chrysalus answers identifying him: son of Megalobulus, now most dear to the Ephesians. Kept both lines of the answer as one contiguous identifying sentence to the full stop; the next line is Nicobulus's own reaction ('Ne ille hercle mihi sit multo tanto carior').
